summary: Grassy Knob's 10x10 ft cab, built in 1934 and gone by the 1960s, leaves four guy-cable anchors on a short hike east of Port Orford.

facts.design: 10 by 10 ft cab; an Oregon Lookouts note gives a lookout house on a 12-foot tower
facts.status_note: Only four guy-cable anchors remain, per Oregon Hikers

access.note: Reached by a short hike up an old lookout road into a Coast Range wilderness; no closure is reported in these sources

visit.trail_note: A narrow stone staircase leads up to the old lookout site; no structure remains

events.note: 10x10 ft cab per FFLOS and firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts dates a lookout house on a 12-foot tower to 1935
Staffed 79 days; reports relayed to the Gold Beach station by telephone
Activated March 21, 1942 under the Roseburg Filter Center

Lookout reported an airplane motor, a flash and a fire that was controlled, on September 28; the year is disputed (Oregon Hikers says 1942; the Oregon Lookouts page dates its newspaper item June 2, 1943)
Sources give only the 1960s: FFLOS says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed. The year shown is the start of that decade.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS, firelookout.com and Oregon Hikers give 1934 for the cab; Oregon Lookouts gives 1935 for a lookout house on a 12-foot tower. The record uses 1934 and the story reports the 1935 note.
FFLOS says the cab was removed in the 1960s and firelookout.com says it was destroyed then. Both agree on the decade; neither gives a year.
Oregon Hikers puts the incendiary-plane sighting in 1942; the Oregon Lookouts page dates its newspaper account June 2, 1943. The story says the year is not settled.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 3.7 m height matches the 12-foot tower in the Oregon Lookouts note, while the FFLOS and firelookout.com pages describe a 10x10 ft cab; I kept 3.7 m as the height. Build year (1934 vs 1935) and incident year (1942 vs the June 1943 newspaper date) are unresolved. The Oregon Lookouts page is a compiled history with dated extracts, so its year labels may be off. The access note rests on the Oregon Hikers description; no official access source was checked. The brief's events list is otherwise accurate.
